articles.title: Do We Really Need Reflection or Code Generation for JSON in Kotlin? Building a Lightweight JSON Library
articles.excerpt: Building a lightweight Kotlin/JVM JSON library with a direct JSON representation and optional reflection-based mapping between JSON and Kotlin classes. I wanted to investigate how convenient a JSON pa…
articles.body: Building a lightweight Kotlin/JVM JSON library with a direct JSON representation and optional reflection-based mapping between JSON and Kotlin classes. Why another parser library? I wanted to investigate how convenient a JSON parser can be when it doesn't require any reflection or code generation. The main goal was to create a tool with a concise, self-explanatory Kotlin API for building and accessing a JSON representation, which I could conveniently use in Android applications. Another requirement was to keep JSON-to-Kotlin-class mapping in a separate artifact, so applications that don't need reflection don't have to include it. This allows us to choose the approach that fits our use case by including only the required artifact.
articles.author: Alexey Kozyakov

articles.title: I removed my Chinese web font. Every page lost 1 MB
articles.excerpt: First published on yappatyih.com. A system font stack is a list of fonts that are already installed on the reader's device, given to the browser in order of preference, so the page downloads no font a…
articles.body: First published on yappatyih.com . TL;DR A system font stack is a list of fonts that are already installed on the reader's device, given to the browser in order of preference, so the page downloads no font at all. On 2 October 2026 I replaced the Chinese web font on this site, Noto Sans SC, with a system font stack. One Chinese post went from 20 font files and 1,107 KB of fonts to 2 files and 54 KB. The whole page went from 1,464 KB to 318 KB. Its Lighthouse mobile score went from 68 and 73 to 84 and 97 across two runs each. The change is four lines of CSS. What I gave up is one identical look on every device. What it did not fix is below too, because the first live measurement was worse than I expected, and the reason turned out to be mostly the measurement itself.
articles.author: Yap Pat Yih

articles.title: I've never run an AI model on my own machine. This month I will.
articles.excerpt: Hi DEV, I'm Ankan, a CS student. I build whole projects end to end — the code that runs on a tiny chip, the server behind it, and the website on top. One habit I've picked up: I like models I can unde…
articles.body: Hi DEV, I'm Ankan, a CS student. I build whole projects end to end — the code that runs on a tiny chip, the server behind it, and the website on top. One habit I've picked up: I like models I can understand. If I can't look at what a model learned and explain it in plain words, I don't trust it enough to put it in front of people. I also keep a list of the things my projects can't do. A missing feature is fine. A feature that looks real but is actually made up is not. This year's Hacktoberfest theme is AI Belongs to Everyone — open-source AI. That hits the one gap I have. I do train models, but small ones, the kind I can read line by line and check myself. Every time I added an AI feature to something, I just sent a request to someone else's API and hoped the answer was right.
articles.author: Ankan Giri

articles.title: How I built German tax calculators where every number shows its law paragraph (Astro + TypeScript + 68 tests)
articles.excerpt: When my wife and I planned for a baby, I tried to figure out her Elterngeld (German parental allowance). Every calculator I found was a black box: enter numbers, get one result, trust us. None of them…
articles.body: When my wife and I planned for a baby, I tried to figure out her Elterngeld (German parental allowance). Every calculator I found was a black box: enter numbers, get one result, trust us. None of them showed how the number was computed, and several still showed an income limit that was replaced in April 2025. So I built the opposite — a suite of calculators where every step displays its formula, percentage, and the legal paragraph. This post is about the engineering behind it. The core idea: tax law as pure functions German tax law is surprisingly deterministic. § 2c BEEG tells you exactly which deductions to apply, § 32a EStG is literally a piecewise-linear income tax formula.
articles.author: hongtao fang
